title: Either branch operations, payload conversions and conditional composition
explanation: The new manual Iterator::next implementation for Either passes the selected inner iterator state to its next dictionary and returns exactly its Option<Item> with the updated state under the same Either tag. None still retains the returned updated state. Normal item/state helpers assume only the selected inner next result; identical modeled failure/divergence propagate without using the other dictionary. This does not prove arbitrary inner iterator progress, termination, length bounds or fusedness. The new map_either/map_either_with contracts preserve the present variant while replacing its payload with the selected callback result; the context-aware form forwards the original context. Normal results require success only at that actual payload/context, and modeled failure/divergence propagate unchanged. inspect_left/right call the selected borrowed-value callback and return the original modeled self after success; on the other variant they return self without any callback premise. This self-retention is a property of the extracted shared-reference value model and does not certify unchanged observable Rust interior/global state under arbitrary callbacks. For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, the forty-five named APIs have the following value-model contracts. either dispatches only to the callback for the present variant, passing exactly its payload; either_with additionally passes the original context as the first pair element. either_into dispatches that payload to the corresponding Into dictionary. Their main contracts preserve the selected computation's whole modeled Result without assuming success. Separate normal-value contracts need success only at the selected payload/context; failure and divergence helpers retain the same modeled outcome. The unused callback/conversion dictionary is unconstrained. Twelve earlier callback APIs compose a mathematical callback under their explicit normal-result premises for every callback argument, with selected failure propagated and nonselected results preserved. The real impl<T> IntoEither for T dictionary is linked to its original default, so into_either_with requires only normal predicate behavior at the actual borrowed input. Predicates/projections identify and retain the exact variant and optional payload; flip swaps it and flipping twice reconstructs the original. Eager selection preserves the indicated payload or supplied alternative. Optional and tuple factoring preserve tags and exact components. as_ref preserves the borrowed view; as_mut's backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back. The original handwritten conversions map Result Ok to Right and Err to Left, with exact payloads, and reverse those mappings; both roundtrips reconstruct every variant. left_or_default/right_or_default preserve the matching payload without a Default premise and otherwise delegate the Default computation's entire modeled outcome. Normal fallback values, modeled failure and divergence have separate explicit premises. The earlier thirty APIs return normally in this model under their stated conditions; the Default fallback pair and the three dispatch APIs retain abstract selected-computation outcomes. These are value-semantic guarantees with the destructor and callback boundaries stated below. Separate supplemental Lean proofs cover the original shared-reference and mutable-reference specialized copied/cloned methods. copied preserves the selected branch and payload; mutable copied also preserves both extracted backward-state values. cloned delegates exactly to the selected Clone dictionary, preserving its modeled Result including failure/divergence, and wraps a successful clone in the same branch. Mutable cloned additionally preserves the two extracted backward-model values. These four specialized Rust methods are not registered machine claims because source-scanner specialized-owner matching remains blocked; the primary mappings remain separate. The original DoubleEndedIterator::next_back method exactly delegates to the selected inner dictionary, returning its Option and updated state in the same Either branch and preserving modeled failure or divergence. This contract imposes no independent iterator correctness or termination law. Two additional original conversions delegate to only the selected IntoIterator dictionary. factor_into_iter permits distinct left/right Item types and wraps the returned iterator in the original IterEither; into_iter requires equal Item types while allowing distinct IntoIter types and wraps directly in the same Either branch. The exact equations preserve all modeled Result outcomes, including callback failure/divergence and modeled visible effects. These contracts do not verify operations of the produced iterator or arbitrary callback behavior. The original shared-reference iter method is additionally verified under its higher-ranked borrowed IntoIterator dictionaries. For every modeled shared input it invokes only the selected shared-reference dictionary, whose exact Result is wrapped in the same Either branch. The original bounds require borrowed inputs for every lifetime, equal Item and independently typed returned iterators; they do not assert that the owned payloads implement IntoIterator. The original shared-reference factor_iter is additionally verified under higher-ranked borrowed IntoIterator dictionaries with independent left/right Item and IntoIter types. Only the selected borrowed callback is invoked; its exact Result is wrapped through the original IterEither constructor. In the Rust type, IterEither combines the two item families as Either<LItem,RItem>, so no equality of left/right Item is required. This contract concerns callback delegation and construction, not the behavior of iterator next or sequence laws.
trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library value models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are restricted to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No additional axioms or custom models are used. Generic FnOnce, Into, IntoIterator and Default computations are explicit dictionary parameters; their concrete implementations and effects are not independently verified here. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value/backward-function semantics and do not independently prove the Rust borrow checker or aliasing model. The reference4 supplement uses the same official pinned translation with a separate official namespace. Its six theorems use only the standard Lean axioms. Clone dictionary correspondence is conditional; no law that clone output equals input is assumed.
environment: Official pinned Charon/Aeneas extraction of unchanged either1.19.0 source uses46 ordered selectors and one Generated Either/IterEither primary type environment. All45 source-bound primary mappings import in thirteen proof modules, with148 distinct primary/helper theorem audits using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The reference4 supplement remains six conditional model theorems in a separate library, reached by the explicit needs leanArts facet; its conflicting global discriminant environment is not coimported. The original archive/tests and ordered Lean/translation JSON regeneration are preserved. The current union keeps every old44 mapping field and twelve proof sources unchanged and adds only shared factor_iter. Small preparation notes are historical and superseded by completed kernel/union evidence. Mutable iter_mut remains unsupported and is not included.
limitations: Iterator::next writeback is a value/backward-state model guarantee under the supplied inner next dictionary, not verification of that concrete iterator or all Rust memory/external effects. No size_hint/len/count, finite-length or fused-iterator guarantee is added. For inspect_left/right, returning self in the extracted model must not be read as proving that callbacks cannot mutate interior/global state or that physical Rust payloads stay observationally unchanged. Only the forty-five mapped callables and their stated composition helpers are verified, not every public API. The new dispatch contracts establish branch/payload/context forwarding and modeled Result delegation, not arbitrary callback or Into correctness, success, termination, panic freedom or captured-state effects. Their normal-value theorems assume the selected call succeeds at that argument. No arbitrary mutable-context writeback or eager argument-construction claim is added. Rust Drop for discarded callbacks/payloads can panic, diverge or affect global state; destructor execution, unwind/return ordering, resource consumption and external effects are outside the value model. Modeled fail/div propagation is not a specification of every Rust panic payload or unwinding behavior. Default implementation values/termination/effects remain unverified. IntoEither uses the actual blanket dispatch, but its predicate/reference semantics retain the stated model boundary. Other inherent methods, iterator and pinning APIs, most trait/blanket implementations and serde remain unproved. into_inner still fails the untouched generated Lean do-match elaborator for the repeated T parameter; factor_ok/factor_err remain blocked by their current extraction/model limitations. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets are not proved. The four reference-method results are supplementary model proofs only; ambiguous nominal source keys are not substituted for exact shared/mutable receiver identities. They do not guarantee arbitrary Clone correctness or termination, interior/global state preservation, Drop/panic/unwinding, external effects or physical aliasing/lifetimes. Backward-value equalities are not independent Rust memory proofs. The supplemental model and primary model are compiled in separate Lean module environments because their generated global discriminant-instance names collide on simultaneous import; no simultaneous model-equivalence bridge is claimed. The primary mappings now number45; next_back retains the selected dictionary and value-model assumptions, without arbitrary iterator termination, Drop/panic/unwinding, interior/global effect or independent memory guarantees. The two conversion contracts do not establish Iterator laws, callback correctness/termination, concrete iterator next/size_hint behavior, arbitrary Rust Drop/interior-mutability/global effects or independent heap/alias/provenance. The normal result depends only on the selected IntoIterator callback returning that value. IterEither operations with unresolved extraction assumptions are not verified by constructing the wrapper. The shared iter contract preserves the represented callback Result, including model failure/divergence/visible effects, but does not establish concrete callback correctness or termination, iterator laws/operations, physical shared-reference identity or lifetime/alias safety, or arbitrary Rust Drop/interior-mutability/global effects. iter_mut remains unsupported because its official generated backward-pair use does not match the standard dictionary result type; no mutable mapping or model repair is claimed. The factor_iter result does not establish callback correctness or termination, produced iterator operations/ordering, physical shared-reference identity or lifetime/alias safety, or arbitrary Rust Drop/interior-mutability/global effects. Its two Item families are independent; no additional same-Item condition is imposed. Shared iter retains its own original equal-Item bound. Unsupported mutable iter_mut is still excluded, and constructing IterEither does not prove its next implementation.
tool_limitations: Lean backend only, requiring cargo-proofs 0.4.0 or later. The version identifies the official Aeneas Git revision pinned in lake-manifest.json (backends/lean); this revision uses Lean 4.35.0. The recorder checks committed Lean theorem declarations and permits only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as transitive axioms. It rejects sorryAx and custom axioms, including axiomatized external models. Charon/Aeneas extraction is not rerun. The author must review that the committed functional model matches the recorded Rust source, that the named theorem corresponds to the public API, and that the reported precondition matches the theorem. A checked theorem alone does not establish those links or the adequacy of the specification. The current adapter records the default Cargo configuration, with ordinary Lean module paths and a pinned official Git dependency. Other backends, custom Lake source directories, and local-path Aeneas dependencies are unsupported. See https://proofs.rs/book/aeneas.html and https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/tree/be86ab0f1989d04944292b345b24c435be3ad10a.

impl<L, R> Either<L, R>

claims.report_title: Either branch operations, payload conversions and conditional composition
claims.shared_explanation: The new manual Iterator::next implementation for Either passes the selected inner iterator state to its next dictionary and returns exactly its Option<Item> with the updated state under the same Either tag. None still retains the returned updated state. Normal item/state helpers assume only the selected inner next result; identical modeled failure/divergence propagate without using the other dictionary. This does not prove arbitrary inner iterator progress, termination, length bounds or fusedness. The new map_either/map_either_with contracts preserve the present variant while replacing its payload with the selected callback result; the context-aware form forwards the original context. Normal results require success only at that actual payload/context, and modeled failure/divergence propagate unchanged. inspect_left/right call the selected borrowed-value callback and return the original modeled self after success; on the other variant they return self without any callback premise. This self-retention is a property of the extracted shared-reference value model and does not certify unchanged observable Rust interior/global state under arbitrary callbacks. For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, the forty-five named APIs have the following value-model contracts. either dispatches only to the callback for the present variant, passing exactly its payload; either_with additionally passes the original context as the first pair element. either_into dispatches that payload to the corresponding Into dictionary. Their main contracts preserve the selected computation's whole modeled Result without assuming success. Separate normal-value contracts need success only at the selected payload/context; failure and divergence helpers retain the same modeled outcome. The unused callback/conversion dictionary is unconstrained. Twelve earlier callback APIs compose a mathematical callback under their explicit normal-result premises for every callback argument, with selected failure propagated and nonselected results preserved. The real impl<T> IntoEither for T dictionary is linked to its original default, so into_either_with requires only normal predicate behavior at the actual borrowed input. Predicates/projections identify and retain the exact variant and optional payload; flip swaps it and flipping twice reconstructs the original. Eager selection preserves the indicated payload or supplied alternative. Optional and tuple factoring preserve tags and exact components. as_ref preserves the borrowed view; as_mut's backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back. The original handwritten conversions map Result Ok to Right and Err to Left, with exact payloads, and reverse those mappings; both roundtrips reconstruct every variant. left_or_default/right_or_default preserve the matching payload without a Default premise and otherwise delegate the Default computation's entire modeled outcome. Normal fallback values, modeled failure and divergence have separate explicit premises. The earlier thirty APIs return normally in this model under their stated conditions; the Default fallback pair and the three dispatch APIs retain abstract selected-computation outcomes. These are value-semantic guarantees with the destructor and callback boundaries stated below. Separate supplemental Lean proofs cover the original shared-reference and mutable-reference specialized copied/cloned methods. copied preserves the selected branch and payload; mutable copied also preserves both extracted backward-state values. cloned delegates exactly to the selected Clone dictionary, preserving its modeled Result including failure/divergence, and wraps a successful clone in the same branch. Mutable cloned additionally preserves the two extracted backward-model values. These four specialized Rust methods are not registered machine claims because source-scanner specialized-owner matching remains blocked; the primary mappings remain separate. The original DoubleEndedIterator::next_back method exactly delegates to the selected inner dictionary, returning its Option and updated state in the same Either branch and preserving modeled failure or divergence. This contract imposes no independent iterator correctness or termination law. Two additional original conversions delegate to only the selected IntoIterator dictionary. factor_into_iter permits distinct left/right Item types and wraps the returned iterator in the original IterEither; into_iter requires equal Item types while allowing distinct IntoIter types and wraps directly in the same Either branch. The exact equations preserve all modeled Result outcomes, including callback failure/divergence and modeled visible effects. These contracts do not verify operations of the produced iterator or arbitrary callback behavior. The original shared-reference iter method is additionally verified under its higher-ranked borrowed IntoIterator dictionaries. For every modeled shared input it invokes only the selected shared-reference dictionary, whose exact Result is wrapped in the same Either branch. The original bounds require borrowed inputs for every lifetime, equal Item and independently typed returned iterators; they do not assert that the owned payloads implement IntoIterator. The original shared-reference factor_iter is additionally verified under higher-ranked borrowed IntoIterator dictionaries with independent left/right Item and IntoIter types. Only the selected borrowed callback is invoked; its exact Result is wrapped through the original IterEither constructor. In the Rust type, IterEither combines the two item families as Either<LItem,RItem>, so no equality of left/right Item is required. This contract concerns callback delegation and construction, not the behavior of iterator next or sequence laws.
claims.shared_trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library value models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are restricted to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No additional axioms or custom models are used. Generic FnOnce, Into, IntoIterator and Default computations are explicit dictionary parameters; their concrete implementations and effects are not independently verified here. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value/backward-function semantics and do not independently prove the Rust borrow checker or aliasing model. The reference4 supplement uses the same official pinned translation with a separate official namespace. Its six theorems use only the standard Lean axioms. Clone dictionary correspondence is conditional; no law that clone output equals input is assumed.
claims.shared_limitations: Iterator::next writeback is a value/backward-state model guarantee under the supplied inner next dictionary, not verification of that concrete iterator or all Rust memory/external effects. No size_hint/len/count, finite-length or fused-iterator guarantee is added. For inspect_left/right, returning self in the extracted model must not be read as proving that callbacks cannot mutate interior/global state or that physical Rust payloads stay observationally unchanged. Only the forty-five mapped callables and their stated composition helpers are verified, not every public API. The new dispatch contracts establish branch/payload/context forwarding and modeled Result delegation, not arbitrary callback or Into correctness, success, termination, panic freedom or captured-state effects. Their normal-value theorems assume the selected call succeeds at that argument. No arbitrary mutable-context writeback or eager argument-construction claim is added. Rust Drop for discarded callbacks/payloads can panic, diverge or affect global state; destructor execution, unwind/return ordering, resource consumption and external effects are outside the value model. Modeled fail/div propagation is not a specification of every Rust panic payload or unwinding behavior. Default implementation values/termination/effects remain unverified. IntoEither uses the actual blanket dispatch, but its predicate/reference semantics retain the stated model boundary. Other inherent methods, iterator and pinning APIs, most trait/blanket implementations and serde remain unproved. into_inner still fails the untouched generated Lean do-match elaborator for the repeated T parameter; factor_ok/factor_err remain blocked by their current extraction/model limitations. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets are not proved. The four reference-method results are supplementary model proofs only; ambiguous nominal source keys are not substituted for exact shared/mutable receiver identities. They do not guarantee arbitrary Clone correctness or termination, interior/global state preservation, Drop/panic/unwinding, external effects or physical aliasing/lifetimes. Backward-value equalities are not independent Rust memory proofs. The supplemental model and primary model are compiled in separate Lean module environments because their generated global discriminant-instance names collide on simultaneous import; no simultaneous model-equivalence bridge is claimed. The primary mappings now number45; next_back retains the selected dictionary and value-model assumptions, without arbitrary iterator termination, Drop/panic/unwinding, interior/global effect or independent memory guarantees. The two conversion contracts do not establish Iterator laws, callback correctness/termination, concrete iterator next/size_hint behavior, arbitrary Rust Drop/interior-mutability/global effects or independent heap/alias/provenance. The normal result depends only on the selected IntoIterator callback returning that value. IterEither operations with unresolved extraction assumptions are not verified by constructing the wrapper. The shared iter contract preserves the represented callback Result, including model failure/divergence/visible effects, but does not establish concrete callback correctness or termination, iterator laws/operations, physical shared-reference identity or lifetime/alias safety, or arbitrary Rust Drop/interior-mutability/global effects. iter_mut remains unsupported because its official generated backward-pair use does not match the standard dictionary result type; no mutable mapping or model repair is claimed. The factor_iter result does not establish callback correctness or termination, produced iterator operations/ordering, physical shared-reference identity or lifetime/alias safety, or arbitrary Rust Drop/interior-mutability/global effects. Its two Item families are independent; no additional same-Item condition is imposed. Shared iter retains its own original equal-Item bound. Unsupported mutable iter_mut is still excluded, and constructing IterEither does not prove its next implementation.
claims.environment: Official pinned Charon/Aeneas extraction of unchanged either1.19.0 source uses46 ordered selectors and one Generated Either/IterEither primary type environment. All45 source-bound primary mappings import in thirteen proof modules, with148 distinct primary/helper theorem audits using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The reference4 supplement remains six conditional model theorems in a separate library, reached by the explicit needs leanArts facet; its conflicting global discriminant environment is not coimported. The original archive/tests and ordered Lean/translation JSON regeneration are preserved. The current union keeps every old44 mapping field and twelve proof sources unchanged and adds only shared factor_iter. Small preparation notes are historical and superseded by completed kernel/union evidence. Mutable iter_mut remains unsupported and is not included.
claims.tool_limitations: Lean backend only, requiring cargo-proofs 0.4.0 or later. The version identifies the official Aeneas Git revision pinned in lake-manifest.json (backends/lean); this revision uses Lean 4.35.0. The recorder checks committed Lean theorem declarations and permits only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as transitive axioms. It rejects sorryAx and custom axioms, including axiomatized external models. Charon/Aeneas extraction is not rerun. The author must review that the committed functional model matches the recorded Rust source, that the named theorem corresponds to the public API, and that the reported precondition matches the theorem. A checked theorem alone does not establish those links or the adequacy of the specification. The current adapter records the default Cargo configuration, with ordinary Lean module paths and a pinned official Git dependency. Other backends, custom Lake source directories, and local-path Aeneas dependencies are unsupported. See https://proofs.rs/book/aeneas.html and https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/tree/be86ab0f1989d04944292b345b24c435be3ad10a.

Separate normal-value contracts need success only at the selected payload/context; failure and divergence helpers retain the same modeled outcome. Predicates/projections identify and retain the exact variant and optional payload; flip swaps it and flipping twice reconstructs the original. Eager selection preserves the indicated payload or supplied alternative. Optional and tuple factoring preserve tags and exact components. as_ref preserves the borrowed view; as_mut's backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back. claims.shared_explanation: The new manual Iterator::next implementation for Either passes the selected inner iterator state to its next dictionary and returns exactly its Option<Item> with the updated state under the same Either tag. None still retains the returned updated state. Normal item/state helpers assume only the selected inner next result; identical modeled failure/divergence propagate without using the other dictionary. This does not prove arbitrary inner iterator progress, termination, length bounds or fusedness. The new map_either/map_either_with contracts preserve the present variant while replacing its payload with the selected callback result; the context-aware form forwards the original context. Normal results require success only at that actual payload/context, and modeled failure/divergence propagate unchanged. inspect_left/right call the selected borrowed-value callback and return the original modeled self after success; on the other variant they return self without any callback premise. This self-retention is a property of the extracted shared-reference value model and does not certify unchanged observable Rust interior/global state under arbitrary callbacks. For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, the forty-five named APIs have the following value-model contracts. either dispatches only to the callback for the present variant, passing exactly its payload; either_with additionally passes the original context as the first pair element. either_into dispatches that payload to the corresponding Into dictionary. Their main contracts preserve the selected computation's whole modeled Result without assuming success. Separate normal-value contracts need success only at the selected payload/context; failure and divergence helpers retain the same modeled outcome. The unused callback/conversion dictionary is unconstrained. Twelve earlier callback APIs compose a mathematical callback under their explicit normal-result premises for every callback argument, with selected failure propagated and nonselected results preserved. The real impl<T> IntoEither for T dictionary is linked to its original default, so into_either_with requires only normal predicate behavior at the actual borrowed input. Predicates/projections identify and retain the exact variant and optional payload; flip swaps it and flipping twice reconstructs the original. Eager selection preserves the indicated payload or supplied alternative. Optional and tuple factoring preserve tags and exact components. as_ref preserves the borrowed view; as_mut's backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back. The original handwritten conversions map Result Ok to Right and Err to Left, with exact payloads, and reverse those mappings; both roundtrips reconstruct every variant. left_or_default/right_or_default preserve the matching payload without a Default premise and otherwise delegate the Default computation's entire modeled outcome. Normal fallback values, modeled failure and divergence have separate explicit premises. The earlier thirty APIs return normally in this model under their stated conditions; the Default fallback pair and the three dispatch APIs retain abstract selected-computation outcomes. These are value-semantic guarantees with the destructor and callback boundaries stated below. Separate supplemental Lean proofs cover the original shared-reference and mutable-reference specialized copied/cloned methods. copied preserves the selected branch and payload; mutable copied also preserves both extracted backward-state values. cloned delegates exactly to the selected Clone dictionary, preserving its modeled Result including failure/divergence, and wraps a successful clone in the same branch. Mutable cloned additionally preserves the two extracted backward-model values. These four specialized Rust methods are not registered machine claims because source-scanner specialized-owner matching remains blocked; the primary mappings remain separate. The original DoubleEndedIterator::next_back method exactly delegates to the selected inner dictionary, returning its Option and updated state in the same Either branch and preserving modeled failure or divergence. This contract imposes no independent iterator correctness or termination law. Two additional original conversions delegate to only the selected IntoIterator dictionary. factor_into_iter permits distinct left/right Item types and wraps the returned iterator in the original IterEither; into_iter requires equal Item types while allowing distinct IntoIter types and wraps directly in the same Either branch. The exact equations preserve all modeled Result outcomes, including callback failure/divergence and modeled visible effects. These contracts do not verify operations of the produced iterator or arbitrary callback behavior. The original shared-reference iter method is additionally verified under its higher-ranked borrowed IntoIterator dictionaries. For every modeled shared input it invokes only the selected shared-reference dictionary, whose exact Result is wrapped in the same Either branch. The original bounds require borrowed inputs for every lifetime, equal Item and independently typed returned iterators; they do not assert that the owned payloads implement IntoIterator. The original shared-reference factor_iter is additionally verified under higher-ranked borrowed IntoIterator dictionaries with independent left/right Item and IntoIter types. Only the selected borrowed callback is invoked; its exact Result is wrapped through the original IterEither constructor. In the Rust type, IterEither combines the two item families as Either<LItem,RItem>, so no equality of left/right Item is required. This contract concerns callback delegation and construction, not the behavior of iterator next or sequence laws.

claims.tool_limitations: Lean backend only, requiring cargo-proofs 0.4.0 or later.
